files.role: Manifest body and separate index-section readers, mutable manifest serialization to an already-open Writer, and legacy schema-only ManifestProvider. Owns low-level metadata IO/framing interpretation, not dataset capability validation, commit arbitration or footer/shutdown publication.
ranges: SPDX and imports bind async_trait, LittleEndian, Bytes/Buf, fallible streams, exact storage version and legacy V1 dictionary/provider helpers, object-store paths/extensions, Prost, collections/Arc, tracing, core Schema/Error, lance-io Writer extensions/chunk utilities, table metadata/protobuf/MAGIC and ManifestLocation. Public io module exposes this child; no environment variables or global mutable state here.

Public async read_manifest(store,path,known_size) reads manifest files only. Debug instrumentation skips store. Supplied u64 size bypasses explicit HEAD; absent size awaits inner.head. PREFETCH_SIZE is64*1024 bytes; saturating_sub chooses tail start and one inner.get_range fetches through supplied/observed end. GET errors propagate immediately; it does not verify supplied size first or read data files.

Only a successfully returned tail shorter than16 or lacking trailing table MAGIC triggers one recursive boxed retry without cached size. Retry has None so cannot recurse again. If still short or wrong magic, CorruptFile includes path and reason. Arbitrary range/HEAD errors, bad offset, bad length or protobuf decode do not trigger this retry. Footer major/minor bytes are not inspected by these checks.

Read footer offset as signed little-endian i64 then unchecked as usize; file_size is also unchecked cast to usize before ordinary subtraction. No explicit negative/out-of-file offset validation. If computed manifest_len fits tail, slice from its computed start; else open a sized reader. Corrupt offsets can cause arithmetic/slicing failures rather than contextual Result errors; this is source-level observation, not an executed repro.

Large-body path fetches manifest_pos through file_size-64KiB in METADATA_READ_CHUNK_SIZE chunks, accumulating every Bytes in ChunkedBuf, then appends prefetched tail. Requires combined remaining>=20, reads u32 LE prefix, truncates trailing16, and returns decode_manifest. Errors drop local buffer/futures; no write. Contextual helper uses16MiB chunks with ordered buffered concurrency max(reader.io_parallelism,1); chunk handles avoid whole-body concatenation but all bytes remain resident for decode (rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:27-95). Comment throughput/memory motivations are not measurements performed here.

Fast path reads prefix buf[0..4], slices4..len-16 and delegates; unlike chunk branch no explicit20-byte minimum after trimming. Private decode_manifest requires exact remaining==recorded_length or InvalidInput with expected/actual sizes, then Prost decode, Manifest::try_from and sparse-inline-row-ID detach heuristic using message-body length. No capability/feature/footer-version validation occurs here. Length mismatch lacks path argument; conversion/decode errors propagate. Byte detachment may copy small inline payloads after otherwise shared decoding.

Public async read_manifest_indexes(store,location,manifest) reads only when index_section Some; absent returns empty Vec without opening storage. On read_index_section error, retry once without cached size only if location.size Some and error.to_string contains exact file size is too small substring. Other errors propagate. Convert all returned protobuf entries in order, failing whole Result on first metadata conversion error. No independent count/UUID/type/capability validation here; None and encoded empty section both return empty Vec.

Private read_index_section opens with unchecked u64->usize sized hint when Some, otherwise normal open, then awaits generic read_message at pos. Underlying helper validates length-prefix/body against reader.size and emits the retry substring for a too-small sized view (rust/lance-io/src/utils.rs:161-199). This wrapper does not read footer or verify offset belongs to an IndexSection.

Private do_write_manifest borrows mutable Writer/Manifest, owns optional index Vec and optional inline transaction. Some indices (even empty) converts entire vector into pb::IndexSection, awaits write_protobuf and then updates manifest.index_section to returned position. None explicitly clears inherited index_section so stale offsets cannot refer to unrelated bytes. A failed write may leave bytes partly emitted; local code supplies no rollback.

If transaction Some, take/move wrapper into pb::Transaction, await write_protobuf then set transaction_section; None clears inherited offset. Finally write_struct serializes current manifest and returns its starting offset. Earlier index/transaction writes and in-memory offset mutations survive later failure/cancellation; no footer, flush, shutdown, feature checks, CAS or cleanup in this helper. Transaction wrapper conversion itself is a move, while protobuf writer allocates encoding buffer (rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:53-63; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:84-92).

Public write_manifest on an open dyn Writer branches only on exact manifest default storage version: V1 awaits write_schema_dictionaries mutating schema, every V2_0/1/2/3 skips that step. Then delegate do_write_manifest. Legacy dictionary route is compatibility behavior, not a general new-format implementation hook. Return usize is metadata starting position, not byte count; caller must append footer and close writer.

Public empty ManifestDescribing implements legacy V1ManifestProvider::store_schema asynchronously. Clone schema into new Manifest with no fragments/bases and explicit V1; directly call do_write_manifest with no index/transaction and return Some(position). It bypasses write_manifest dictionary step because provider delegates only schema-envelope writing at this boundary. No inherent constructor/Default or public fields beyond empty struct.

Private cfg(test) module imports Arrow arrays/batches/schema, SelfDescribingFileReader, legacy FileReader/FileWriter and lance-file footer constants, random alphanumerics and tokio AsyncWriteExt. Tests below use in-memory stores and were read, not run. Imported footer major/minor are lance-file's0/2, not table facade's0/1; reader only checks magic/position here.

Roundtrip helper creates memory store/path, writes random alphanumeric prefix of requested length, makes deterministic repeated-a field name at least requested payload size and constructs default-format empty-fragment manifest. Builds config key/value map but never attaches it to manifest, so this fixture does not test persisted config values. Size inflation is schema-name content, not many fragments or dictionaries.

Roundtrip helper writes body, explicitly appends footer, explicitly shuts down, reads with unknown size and asserts full Manifest equality, then deletes object. This pins sequence of body/footer/close in test but not production commit arbitration or known-size retry behavior.

test_read_large_manifest invokes helper with prefix/body sizes(0,100000),(1000,100000),(1000,1000). Separate larger-than-chunk case uses1000-byte prefix and METADATA_READ_CHUNK_SIZE+4MiB filler, i.e.20MiB with contextual16MiB constant. They cover whole-tail, extra-range and multi-chunk shapes; no timing/peak-memory assertions or injected concurrency failures.

Clears-unwritten-index test sets index_section Some42, writes with indices/transaction None, adds footer/shuts down, then asserts in-memory and reread index_section None. It does not test inherited transaction_section clearing, Some(empty) indices, failed writes or retry on stale known size.

Legacy schema metadata test writes one Int32 i batch0..10 through V1FileWriter<ManifestDescribing>, finish_with_metadata adds lance:extra=for_test, opens self-described V1 reader and checks Arrow schema metadata value. Exercises legacy provider integration with fresh current writer, not released historical fixtures or v2 metadata. Closing brace ends module/file.

This IO layer is not complete storage commit, feature-gate validation or released-format compatibility qualification; unchecked malformed-footer boundaries are static observations only.

files.role: Physical deletion-vector path construction, whole-object Arrow IPC/Roaring serialization and deserialization, audit tracing and local memory-store regression tests. Operates on u32 row offsets for caller-supplied fragment/base, not logical row IDs or transactional manifest publication.
ranges: SPDX/imports HashSet,Arc,LazyLock; Arrow UInt32Array/batches/IPC ZSTD reader-writer/schema errors; Bytes Buf; core errors/DeletionVector/audit labels; object store, Path, RNG, Roaring, Snafu and tracing. Existing HashSet use reflects actual implementation despite general repository preference for Roaring. No feature gate or per-module config declaration.

Public DELETIONS_DIR exactly _deletions. Private LazyLock<SchemaRef> initializes one nonnullable UInt32 field named row_id. Despite name these values are physical offsets, not u64 stable IDs. Protobuf comment says Int32Array whereas implementation schema/array are UInt32 (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:251-268); preserve discrepancy, do not silently rewrite either contract.

Public deletion_file_path(base,fragment_id,metadata) destructures read_version/random id/file_type, gets suffix arrow/bin and joins base/_deletions/{fragment}-{read_version}-{id}.{suffix}. Returns Path rooted at supplied base, despite doc saying relative to dataset root. Ignores num_deleted_rows and base_id; caller resolves external base/store. No validation or IO.

Public relative_deletion_file_path creates exact relative String _deletions/{fragment}-{read_version}-{id}.{suffix}. Same metadata fields/suffix; supplied base not involved, base_id ignored. Used by contextual operation diagnostics, not independently a resolver.

Public async write_deletion_file borrows base/DeletionVector/store, accepts u64 fragment/read version and returns Option<DeletionFile>. Match NoDeletions=>None without storage calls. Set arm generates random u64 id, Array metadata, Some(set.len()) and base_idNone, then builds path. It does not normalize Set(empty) to no file, check physical row bounds or reserve collision-free IDs; comment no deletions returnsNone is strictly the enum arm, not generic emptiness.

Set write iterates HashSet in unspecified order into UInt32Array, Arc and one RecordBatch with fixed schema. Allocate full Vec<u8>; configure Arrow IPC default options with ZSTD, write one batch and finish IPC synchronously, drop writer to release Vec borrow, then await object_store.put. Successful put precedes create audit info and Some(metadata). Errors before put have no object effect; put error/cancellation outcome/cleanup depend on store. No explicit sorting, streaming, row validation or transaction commit here.

Bitmap arm independently creates random ID and Bitmap metadata with len as usize, serializes Roaring directly into full Vec, awaits put and logs creation after success. Does not call run_optimize or add custom footer/compression framing. Empty bitmap is still written; no conversion based on density at this boundary. Serialization error propagates; metadata returned only after put succeeds. Both branches leave input vector borrowed/unchanged.

Public async read_deletion_file debug instrumentation skips base/store arguments but explicitly records base and later bytes_read. Dispatch from metadata.file_type. Array path reads whole object, records raw byte count, wraps cursor, builds Arrow IPC reader and collects all batches before shape check. Batch iteration errors are boxed and reclassified CorruptFile(path); Arrow reader-construction error propagates through generic conversion, without this explicit path wrapper. Memory includes full bytes plus all decoded batches.

Require exactly one decoded RecordBatch or CorruptFile including count. Pop unwrap is guarded by len1. Require exact schema equality with fixed LazyLock schema or contextual CorruptFile; equality includes field name/type/nullability and metadata, not only one integer column. This rejects signed Int32 even though protobuf comment uses it. No metadata.num_deleted_rows check is done.

Access column0 and downcast UInt32 with unwrap after schema check. Allocate HashSet capacity equal array length; insert every Some value, deduplicating repeated offsets; any null returns CorruptFile(path). Return Set directly even if empty, with no density selection or normalization to NoDeletions. No fragment physical-row bound or count-versus-metadata validation; accepted values can span u32 domain.

Bitmap path reads all bytes, records length, creates Bytes reader and calls Roaring deserialize_from. Decode failures boxed as CorruptFile(path); success returns Bitmap as read. Caller does not inspect remaining trailing bytes, optimize representation, verify metadata count or physical bounds. Whether decoder consumes/rejects extra bytes is dependency behavior, not checked by this function. No global cache here.

Private cfg(test) imports parent and ObjectStoreExt. NoDeletions test constructs memory URI, writes fragment0/version0 and asserts returnedNone only. Does not list store to prove no object, or test empty Set/Bitmap. Tests were read, not executed.

Array-write test starts explicit Set of0..100,fragment21,readversion12 at /write. Asserts Some(Array), metadata read_version and computed path /write/_deletions/21-12-{random}.arrow. Does not assert random uniqueness, num_deleted_rows, base_id or deterministic byte order.

Array test GETs complete object, uses ArrowFileReader to collect, requires one batch and exact schema, downcasts named row_id, unwraps all values, builds DeletionVector::from_iter and compares set semantics to original. Reads Arrow independently of read_deletion_file, but performs no IPC compression-marker assertion or released-file compatibility check.

Bitmap-write test explicit bitmap0..100,fragment21/version12 at /bitmap. Checks Bitmap variant/read version/exact .bin path, GETs bytes, deserializes Roaring and compares to original consumed iterator collected as bitmap. No invalid-file cases, density threshold, count metadata or buffer-size assertion.

Array roundtrip test explicit Set0..100 at /roundtrip, writes then read_deletion_file with resulting metadata and asserts DeletionVector equality. One fragment, current writer, no deleted-row scan or dataset commit exercised.

Bitmap roundtrip analog uses explicit Bitmap0..100 at /bitmap and exact vector equality after public read. Closes test module/file. All five tests are valid-format local fixtures; no empty variants, NULL/schema mismatch, duplicate offsets, corruption, stale/mismatched count, base relocation or failure/cancellation tests occur here.
